context:
Item-specific guardrails: no unregistered CREATE TABLE rewrites. Tuning must never change query answers.

Shared Exasol guardrails: worktree-only writes with make agent-write-preflight; explicit-path staging, never git add -A; commit identity check, no attribution trailers; uv only; lazy pyexasol import; no credentials in Git, logs, fixtures, or tracker; no live cloud runs; code-skill self-review then make pr-preflight and make pr-open, no auto-merge without make pr-ready; durable artifacts carry no tracker IDs or session narrative; stop and report on failed gates, unverified behavior, license questions, or unapproved host changes.
description:
The adapter core uses no-op tuning hooks. Add Exasol-native tuning: `DISTRIBUTE BY` and `PARTITION BY` in CREATE TABLE or ALTER TABLE, and primary/foreign key constraints with explicit ENABLE/DISABLE state. Exasol enforces constraints by default, so enforcement cost must be controlled.

Tasks:
1. Map BenchBox unified tuning types to Exasol clauses; declare supported tuning types.
2. Apply constraints after load (ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT), with a documented ENABLE/DISABLE policy.
3. Register every CREATE TABLE rewrite under Phase.DDL_OPTIMIZE in benchbox/sql_compat/rules/ddl_optimize/exasol_ddl_rewrites.py and declare constraint capability where BenchBox tracks it (benchbox/sql_compat/ddl_capabilities.py and schema_emit pk_capability rules).
4. Unit tests for clause generation. Run tuned against untuned TPC-H SF 1 locally.

Decision gates:
- G1 Start only with explicit user priority.
- G2 DISTRIBUTE BY has little effect on single-node Personal. If no multi-node target is available, limit the work to constraints and PARTITION BY and document why.
- G3 If enforced constraints change load correctness (rejected rows), stop and report.
